reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Phase 03 correctly identifies that FutureSlot/PastFinalizedSlot data columns return IGNORE without application-level re-queuing, but this is by design and not exploitable. The spec's INV-002 'IGNORE conditions allow re-processing later (queuing)' describes protocol-level behavior (peers may re-gossip), not an implementation requirement for per-node re-processing queues. Lighthouse's implementation is spec-compliant: IGNORE prevents forwarding (correct), and sync mechanisms (UnknownParentDataColumn triggered at L691-693 for ParentUnknown) handle recovery. Blocks that arrive early are queued via EarlyBlock (L1431-1437) because they're already verified and just need delayed import; data columns with FutureSlot fail early validation checks, so re-queuing them would require re-running full validation later, which is unnecessary since peers will re-gossip valid columns when timing is appropriate. The attack scenario assumes attacker can predict exact clock disparity windows, but honest peers re-broadcast columns naturally, and data availability is a network-wide property, not single-node. No availability failures occur in practice because PeerDAS's sampling+reconstruction tolerates transient per-node gaps.
reviewed_items.spec_reference: Spec SG-006 INV-002 describes protocol forwarding semantics (IGNORE = don't forward), not implementation-mandated per-node re-processing queues. Lighthouse correctly implements IGNORE per spec lines 13-15, 22-24.
